svg.title: Predict vs update — one step of the Kalman filter
svg.desc: Prediction steps ahead with the state equation and inflates the variance; the update corrects it with new data and shrinks it. The ratio between them is the Kalman gain.
svg.text: Predict vs update — one step of the Kalman filter
Stepping ahead with the model vs correcting with new data
One step ahead by the model
A large Q makes prediction variance
Observation equation Z, H and y
A large H shrinks the gain, so
less of the observation is used
Previous posterior → a shifted, wider prior
Every step forward means knowing less
A new observation shifts the center and narrows the width
Variance grows at every predict step
With no data this rise simply continues — that is prediction
The gain is the position between prediction and observation
K lies between 0 and 1 — how much to trust each side
Prediction pushes forward what the model knows; the update pulls toward what the data knows.
The two steps alternate, and the variance grows and shrinks in turn.
The update is a weighted average —
Next: when linear-Gaussian assumptions break — EKF, UKF and the particle filter.
